name: DocSend
description: DocSend is a secure document-sharing and virtual data-room platform for controlling access to sensitive files and measuring recipient engagement. Teams use it to share tracked links, manage data rooms, collect signatures, protect documents, and review page-level viewing analytics.
agentUseSummary: DocSend cannot currently be connected as a Relay agent provider because it does not publish a supported delegated account API, OAuth application contract, personal access token, remote MCP service, or authenticated webhook contract. Its supported connected apps are interactive integrations, while its Zapier integration provides four customer-configured outbound triggers rather than a callable DocSend account surface.

blocked.label: Connect a DocSend account
blocked.description: DocSend does not publish a supported OAuth, API-token, remote-MCP, or other delegated account contract for Relay to implement.

blocked.label: Use DocSend account data
blocked.description: Relay cannot truthfully list or change documents, links, visits, analytics, Spaces, permissions, agreements, signatures, contacts, users, or settings without a supported account API.

blocked.label: Treat Zapier triggers as an account API
blocked.description: DocSend's four Zapier triggers are customer-configured outbound events, not provider-authenticated agent tools or a complete callable account surface.

blocked.label: Use unsupported automation
blocked.description: Relay will not automate the DocSend website, reuse browser sessions, reverse-engineer private endpoints, scrape analytics, or relabel Dropbox or Salesforce APIs as DocSend.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled without a supported DocSend delegated account API or distributable provider integration contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No supported DocSend account API is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No supported DocSend account API is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: DocSend publishes interactive connected-app workflows and four Zapier event triggers, but no supported delegated account API, distributable OAuth contract, personal token, remote MCP service, or authenticated webhook schema for a complete Relay agent surface.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request credentials, expose Connect, publish a runtime card, or use private web endpoints. Reconsider DocSend only if Dropbox publishes a supported DocSend account API, remote MCP service, or written distributable integration contract with stable authentication and operation schemas.

evidence.supports: DocSend documents exactly four Zapier triggers—new visit, new link, new Space, and new Space download—and describes Zapier as a no-code alternative to API calls; it does not document callable DocSend actions, account authentication, or stable API schemas.

DocSend's supported connected-app settings list sign-in providers, external cloud storage, Salesforce, and Join.me as interactive user-authorized integrations; no Relay-distributable DocSend developer application or account API is offered.

The official integration catalog covers Dropbox, Google, Outlook, Chrome, Salesforce, mail merge, Zapier, and related user workflows without publishing a DocSend developer API, OAuth scopes, token endpoint, or operation reference.

DocSend's terms prohibit accessing the service by means other than the provided interface unless separately authorized in writing, and prohibit hacking, unauthorized access, and reverse engineering; Relay therefore will not infer or automate private endpoints.

DocSend describes secure tracked links, page-level engagement, Spaces, eSignature, agreements, watermarking, and access controls, establishing the product surface that cannot be represented by the limited trigger-only integration.

Dropbox's official product page brands the same service as Dropbox DocSend and links its secure sharing, analytics, data rooms, NDAs, and eSignature features to DocSend; this is a brand-qualified alias, not a second provider.
